name: two feature update
test:
import torch
X=torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]],dtype=torch.float64); y=torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0],dtype=X.dtype)
w=torch.tensor([0.1, -0.2],dtype=X.dtype); b=X.new_tensor(0.3)
snapshot=[v.clone() for v in (X,y,w,b)]
a,c=linear_regression_step(X,y,w,b,0.05)
assert isinstance(a,torch.Tensor) and isinstance(c,torch.Tensor)
assert a.shape==w.shape and c.shape==()
assert a.dtype==X.dtype and c.dtype==X.dtype and a.device==X.device and c.device==X.device
torch.testing.assert_close(a,X.new_tensor([0.48, 0.34]),rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-12)
torch.testing.assert_close(c,X.new_tensor(0.46),rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-12)
for v,old in zip((X,y,w,b),snapshot): assert torch.equal(v,old)

name: manual gradients preserve dtype device and strided inputs
input: autograd and optimizers disabled; scalar bias and zero learning rate
test:
from contextlib import ExitStack
from unittest.mock import patch
import torch
with ExitStack() as guards:
    for target in ("torch.Tensor.backward", "torch.autograd.grad", "torch.autograd.backward", "torch.optim.SGD", "torch.optim.Adam", "torch.optim.AdamW"):
        guards.enter_context(patch(target, side_effect=AssertionError("Derive gradients and update by hand")))
    devices=['cpu']+(['cuda'] if torch.cuda.is_available() else [])+(['mps'] if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else [])
    for device in devices:
        for dtype in ([torch.float32] if device=='mps' else [torch.float32,torch.float64]):
            X=torch.tensor([[1.,3.,2.,4.],[5.,7.,6.,8.]],dtype=dtype,device=device)[:,::2]
            y=X.new_tensor([2.,3.]); w=X.new_tensor([.2,-.3]); bias=.4
            assert not X.is_contiguous()
            expected_w=w-.05*(2*X.T@(X@w+bias-y)/2)
            expected_b=X.new_tensor(bias)-.05*2*(X@w+bias-y).mean()
            a,b=linear_regression_step(X,y,w,bias,.05)
            assert a.dtype==dtype and b.dtype==dtype and a.device==X.device and b.device==X.device
            torch.testing.assert_close(a,expected_w); torch.testing.assert_close(b,expected_b)
            a,b=linear_regression_step(X,y,w,bias,0.)
            assert torch.equal(a,w) and b==bias
